title: The regulatory surface: abuse reporting across E2EE, and cross-provider consent
description:
Mark, 2026-11-22. DSA-style obligations mean franking and reportAbuse
stop being optional.

ABUSE REPORTING ACROSS E2EE. mimid has franking and the endpoints
(`/v1/reportAbuse/{roomId}`, `Message/reportAbuse` on the agent, and
what a message keeps for a report in mimid-agent-store). The problem is
that the path is UNPROVEN between even two implementations: Haven's live
directory lists `reportAbuse_with_abusive_messages` under `unsupported`,
confirmed from its directory this session. So the part that carries the
actual reported messages has never been exercised cross-implementation.
Reporting abuse across E2EE without the messages is close to useless to
a regulator, since franking is what makes a report verifiable rather
than an accusation.

This is the one the conformance path (mimid-7yn7.1 option B) arguably
cares about MOST: whether a gatekeeper's abuse path really works across
E2EE is exactly the claim a regulator cannot check for itself.

CROSS-PROVIDER CONSENT. mimid has Consent/get, /query and /set on both
the provider and the agent endpoint (the latter added this session, bead
mimid-1wgh.93), and `invites = from-allowed` as the default. The hard
part is not the mechanism: every gatekeeper arrives with its own spam
model, and cross-provider consent SEMANTICS is where that gets ugly.
Concretely, and none of it settled by protocol-07:

- whose consent decision wins when two providers disagree about whether
  contact was allowed;
- whether a consent granted to a user follows them across providers;
- what a provider may infer from a consent request it refuses, which is
  a privacy question, and what it may tell its user about one;
- rate limits, since a consent request is an unsolicited message of a
  kind, and that is exactly the vector a hostile peer would use.

Nothing to implement yet beyond proving reportAbuse with messages works
against a second implementation, which needs Haven to support it. Worth
raising with Jason; posting needs Mark's OK.
